evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires nonempty, differing manager PIDs and invocation IDs before and after. A guest reboot also changes those values, so a reboot can make `manager_restarted` true; the separate `boot_id_changed` check validates only the reboot pair and does not prevent that false positive. This is an implementation defect in the existing feasibility evidence, not a request to enlarge scope. Requiring a nonempty, equal guest boot ID on both manager snapshots closes the conflation.
